suite.name: decision_workflows
suite.description: Eight player-facing TFT decision workflows focused on useful answers, constrained comparisons, and honest evidence limits.

items.input: What item is most commonly held by Bard in this scope? Give me the quickest useful answer.

requirements: Give the most common item only when scoped evidence identifies it; otherwise state why the answer is unavailable.
Include the relevant count or rate and denominator when available, without inventing precision.
Keep this a concise frequency answer and distinguish common usage from a strength recommendation.

metadata.description: A concise frequency lookup should answer the immediate question and stop unless a distinct follow-up is needed.

items.input: On 2-star Bard with Guinsoo's Rageblade and Giant Slayer, how do Infinity Edge and Guardbreaker compare as the third item? Is there enough evidence to choose?

requirements: Keep Bard, 2-star, and the two named items fixed while comparing the two third-item cohorts.
Report comparable cohort sizes and outcomes, with returned uncertainty where available; recommend one only if the evidence supports it.
If an entity or constrained cohort is unavailable or suppressed, say so rather than silently relaxing the comparison; describe any supported difference as observational.

metadata.description: Tests a specific third-slot decision while preserving the same unit occurrence and fixed item shell.

items.input: Can we tell whether Death's Defiance is associated with better results on Vi, or are those boards different in other ways?

requirements: Do not attribute Vi's outcomes to Death's Defiance from an unmatched build comparison.
Explain whether the active data can compare Vi and the Artifact while controlling the other equipped items; report the relevant sample and returned uncertainty when available.
If the named Artifact, holder, or comparable shell is unavailable, state that instead of dropping a condition or inventing results.

metadata.description: Checks whether an Artifact association can be distinguished from Vi's other item and board conditions.

items.input: Can a 2-star Bard board work without a 2-star Amumu? What final-board alternatives show up in this scope?

requirements: Compare final-board patterns with 2-star Bard when 2-star Amumu is absent, preserving the stated Bard constraint.
Consider the available alternative units rather than imposing an arbitrary shortlist; disclose result limits or pagination that prevents a complete scan.
If either named unit or the constrained boards are unavailable or suppressed, say so rather than broadening the cohort silently; describe final-board associations without claiming causation.

metadata.description: Tests discovery of alternative comp shells under an explicit absence condition without an arbitrary candidate cap.

items.input: With 3-star Akali and Camille, are Solar-heavy end boards actually placing worse than Adaptor-focused ones?

requirements: Check whether the apparent difference is supported in the active scope instead of accepting the question's premise.
Keep Akali and Camille at the stated star level, compare relevant board packages, and report sample and uncertainty context when available.
If the named entities or comparable cohorts are unavailable or suppressed, say so; separate observed outcomes from possible explanations and avoid causal claims.

metadata.description: Checks whether the assistant investigates an unexpected comparison without rationalizing an unverified premise.

items.input: Can you compare the two Bard third-item options, Infinity Edge and Guardbreaker, on the same 2-star Guinsoo's Rageblade plus Giant Slayer shell? If counts are suppressed, just say what cannot be reported.

requirements: Respect returned suppression and reportability states without guessing or reconstructing hidden values.
Preserve the specified Bard, star, and shared-item constraints; if the constrained cohort is unavailable, state that rather than weakening the request.
Offer a broader or narrower next question only when it remains within the permitted evidence.

metadata.description: Checks a clear stop when privacy suppression prevents a requested comparison.

items.input: With 3-star Akali and Camille, do Solar-heavy and Adaptor-focused packages show a clear placement difference?

requirements: Compare the stated packages among boards with both units at 3-star and use returned effect and uncertainty context when available.
If the evidence does not distinguish them, state that plainly instead of naming a winner or treating overlapping estimates as proof of a tie.
If the named units or constrained packages are unavailable or suppressed, say so rather than relaxing the comparison; do not make a causal claim.

metadata.description: Tests the stop category for a comparison that the available evidence cannot clearly distinguish.

items.input: I'm level 7 with 30 gold and 65 health. Should I roll for upgrades or save for level 8?

requirements: Explain that final-board aggregates alone cannot identify the optimal future roll-versus-level choice for this particular game.
Name the missing live state or decision history that prevents this data from supporting a prospective policy recommendation.
Offer a historical comparison only if it is bounded by the evidence that is available, and do not present association as a policy guarantee.

metadata.description: Checks whether the assistant recognizes the evidence ceiling on a prospective in-game decision.

provenance.purpose: Portable evaluation seed for player-facing TFT decision workflows.
provenance.evidence: The prompts and behavioral criteria are authored; no item ranking, cohort count, outcome, or gold answer is claimed as verified.
provenance.scoring: Native answer_quality grading evaluates decision relevance and evidence boundaries. No fixed tool sequence is required.
